newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns Japan not to hurt ties over islands.
newsitem.headline: China warns Japan not to hurt ties over islands.

text.p: China on Tuesday urged Japan to prevent Japanese from visiting disputed islands in the East China Sea, saying such incidents could damage Tokyo's relations with Beijing.
Officials in Tokyo said on Monday two Japanese had visited the group of uninhabited islands, known as the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese, which are also claimed by Taiwan.
"The Diaoyu Islands have been Chinese territory since ancient times," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a regular news briefing.
"We demand that the Japanese government adopt measures to prevent further violations of Chinese sovereignty and damage to Sino-Japanese relations," Cui said.

The symbolic visit on Sunday was made as the agricultural ministers of China and Japan prepared to meet in Tokyo to break a deadlock over Japanese plans to declare an exclusive economic zone around the islands.
"We have always stood for resolving the question through talks on the basis of respect for the facts when the time arises," Cui said.

Ownership of the group has galvanised nationalist demonstrations in Japan, China and Taiwan as well as in Hong Kong since Japanese right-wingers built a makeshift lighthouse and planted flags there last July.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
